Intellectual Property & Technology

What the new data rules mean for growing businesses

A practical checklist for founders and boards.

14 October 2026·4 min read

Published
14 October 2026
Practice area
Intellectual Property & Technology
Author
Trueworth
All insights

Data protection rules are getting stricter, and regulators are enforcing them. For a growing business, compliance is now a commercial issue as much as a legal one: investors, partners and large customers increasingly ask to see it.

Start with what you hold

List the personal data the business collects about customers, staff, suppliers and website visitors. For each, note why you hold it, where it is stored and who can access it. Most of the steps below build on this record.

Have a lawful reason for each use

Every use of personal data needs a legal basis, such as consent, a contract or a legitimate business need. Consent is not always the best basis. Where you rely on it, it must be freely given and easy to withdraw.

Tell people what you do

A clear privacy notice on your website and in your sign-up flows should say what you collect, why, how long you keep it and who you share it with.

Secure it, and plan for a breach

Limit access, use strong authentication and encrypt sensitive data. Decide now who does what if data is lost or stolen: many laws set short deadlines for telling the regulator and the people affected.

Check your suppliers

Cloud providers, payroll services and marketing tools all handle your data. Your contracts with them should cover security, confidentiality and what happens to the data when the contract ends, especially where it is stored abroad.

The checklist

  • A record of the personal data you hold
  • A legal basis for each use
  • An up-to-date privacy notice
  • Security measures and a breach plan
  • Data protection terms in supplier contracts
  • A named person responsible for data protection

If you would like to know where your business stands, we can review your current practices and tell you what to fix first.
